mentions.name: qip
mentions.description: A toolchain for writing tiny WebAssembly modules in Zig or C and composing them into pipelines. Modules have a simple input->output interface and run in a strong sandbox with no access to the file system, network, environment variables, or even the time. Modules chain together (e.g., a CommonMark module converts markdown to HTML), and a file-based router serves websites built from these modules. Sites can expose a /view-source page listing all wasm modules, source content (markdown, images, etc.), and source code (Zig, C) so anyone can fork the website's ingredients; the author is also working on collaborative web hosting to bring back web 1.0 vibes.
mentions.problem: The modern web lacks the transparency of 'view source'; qip embraces the ease of copying in an AI coding world by making website ingredients open, inspectable, and forkable.
mentions.audience: Developers who write WebAssembly modules in Zig or C and build websites from composable, forkable modules
mentions.source_excerpt: qip lets you write tiny WebAssembly modules in Zig or C and compose them together. The modules have a simple input -> output interface and cannot access anything else, no file system, no network, no env vars, not even the time.

mentions.name: qip
mentions.description: qip is a CLI for running fast sandboxed WebAssembly modules, designed to safely execute untrusted code generated by LLMs. Modules can be piped from other CLI tools and chained together, with conventions for text, raw bytes, and image shaders. Each module is a pure function with imperative guts, combining probabilistic coding agents with deterministic code.
mentions.problem: Code generated by LLMs is untrusted and may be unsafe (e.g., overflow or try to read ssh keys), so it needs to be run in a sandbox.
mentions.audience: Developers running code generated by LLMs, who need untrusted generated code to execute safely
mentions.source_excerpt: I’m working on qip, a cli for running fast sandboxed WebAssembly modules.
